_comment: #78 What the NPCs say when a hero first sees them on a floor (NpcTalk). first: the lines for a hero meeting the NPC for the first time this run; again: shorter ones for a hero who met it on an earlier floor; freed: a prisoner's line when the cage opens. A line is a string or {text, biome, party}: biome = a floor type id, party = solo / group; lines that don't fit the floor or the party are skipped. {floor} = the floor number, {biome} = the floor's name, {hero} = the hero who sees them. Written to the lore books' rules (#69): plain, concrete, in the speaker's own voice.

archibald.name: Archibald the Gilded
first: Wipe your boots. No, the other boot as well. Now: you have the Key, or you have a reason to be standing at my door.
Floor {floor}. My prices have not gone up since the last one, whatever you may have heard.
Good. Customers who can still walk. Gold on the counter, please, not in the hand.
I buy, I sell, and I do not haggle before noon. Down here it is always before noon.
Do not touch the merchandise in gloves like those. What have you been holding?
You look like people who will need a potion soon. I have potions. They are not cheap.
Mind the step. The last fellow who tripped on it is still paying for the vase.
Everything on these shelves belonged to someone braver than you. That is why it is for sale.
Name, please. For the receipt. I keep the ledger and the ledger keeps me.

first.text: The dead on this level never haggle. A refreshing change. Let us see if you can match them.
Yes, the smell. It comes in under the door. It does not come off the coin.
Do not lean on that wall, it is hot. Everything on this level is hot except the trade.
The archivists upstairs still owe me for a ledger. You are not archivists, I hope.
Barrow gold is old gold. I weigh it twice. Do not take it personally.
Alone? Then you will be carrying everything yourself. Choose light things.
No more than two at the counter, please. The rest of you may admire the stock from the doorway.

again: Back again. Good. The ledger had a gap where you were.
You have the look of someone who sold me something too cheaply.
Welcome back. Same prices. Different floor.
A returning customer. I will pretend to be surprised.
Boots, please.

malphas.name: Malphas the Soul Broker
first: Come in. The door is only rude to those who will not pay it.
All the way down to floor {floor}. That is a long way to carry so much of yourself.
Sit, if you like. Nobody likes. It is a courtesy all the same.
I do not want your gold. Gold is for people who expect to be paid back.
Every contract I offer is fair. I simply read the second page more carefully than you do.
Your health, your sight, your strength. All still there. Splendid. We have something to talk about.
I never lie. It saves a great deal of time, and the truth is usually enough.
Take your time choosing. I have plenty of it, and some of it used to be yours.

first.text: Your companions look worried. Tell them it is only business.
On your own. Then the bargain is entirely between the two of us. I prefer that.
The dead on this level signed nothing. A whole floor wasted, if you ask me.
Mind the water. It is the only thing on this floor that takes without asking.
The Galt Works once bought fire from me. The price is still walking about down here, one arm short.
The archivists here read every clause before they signed. Reading is not the same as understanding.
The barrow kings paid me in grave-goods. You will pay in something warmer.

again: Back so soon? Something from the last bargain stayed with you. Something always does.
Welcome back. Your seat is where you left it.
I wondered when.
Returning is the first clause of every contract.

blacksmith.name: Rolf Hult
first: Shut the door. Heat costs coal, and coal costs blood this far down.
Put it on the bench. No, the bench. The anvil is for iron, not your elbow.
I don't make anything new. I make old things last. It's the better trade.
Floor {floor}. Iron goes soft this deep if you don't keep at it. So do people.
The arm? Made it myself. The first one went in payment for something I never got to use.
Bring me good steel and gold enough, and you'll get it back better. That's the whole of it.
Don't thank me before you've seen the edge. Thank me after it holds.
Everything the dead leave behind wants work. I've the hammer for it.
Twenty years on the casting floor at the Galt Works. This is quieter. Mostly.
Rust I can fix. Curses, take upstairs to someone braver.

first.text: Smell that? Somebody's forge on this level is running cold. Not mine.
Damp gets into the steel here. Oil it, or you'll be carrying a red stick by the next floor.
Old blades in this crypt. Good steel, bad hands. Bring me what you find.
Barrow bronze. Soft as butter, pretty as a wedding. I'll work it if I must.
Paper and dust. Keep my sparks away from your shelves, I learned that one the hard way.
One at a time at the anvil. I've only the one good arm to swing.

again: Back. Show me what you've done to it.
You again. Good. An idle hammer rusts.
Brought me work? Put it down.
Coals are still hot.

prisoner_brann.name: Brann Coldwater
first: Oi. Down here. Before you ask: no, I'm not one of them. I just look it by now.
There's a guard with my key on his belt. Find him, and I'll fight for whoever opens this door.
They took my sword and my boots. The boots I'll miss.
I've been counting the drips. Four thousand and something. Get me out before I lose the number.
My company went on without me. Can't blame them. I'd have done the same, for the right price.
Open this and I'm with you till the stair. No charge. Call it professional courtesy.
Don't look in the bowl. Just don't.
Floor {floor}, is it? I lost count after they hit me.
Watch the one with the key. He swings low.
If you're not letting me out, at least stand where I can see you. The dark plays tricks.
again: Still here. You noticed. Got that key yet?
Same cage, same drips. Same offer.
freed: Right. Where's the nearest thing that needs hitting?
Boots or no boots, I'm with you.

prisoner_ysolde.name: Ysolde Marr
first: Quiet. They come back every so often. Their guard has the key, I watched him put it away.
I tracked something to this floor and it tracked me back. Get me out and I'll show you what.
Three days in here. I've learned their rounds. That's worth a key, I'd say.
My bow's in a pile somewhere with everyone else's. I can shoot with anything.
Don't rattle the bars. The guard likes that.
You came from the stair side? Then the worst is behind you. Or it's still ahead.
I'll keep up. I always keep up.
If they move me, I'll scratch three lines on the floor. Look for them.
Get the key off the big one and I'll owe you a kill. I pay my debts.
Light hurts after this long. Keep your torch low, please.
again: You came back. Most don't.
Still the big one with the key. Still waiting.
freed: Lead on. I'll take the ones behind us.
I owe you a kill. I'll pay it twice.

prisoner_teodor.name: Teodor Vane
first: Visitors with keys? No. Visitors who might get keys. That will do.
I came down to measure the wards on this level. The wards measured me first.
The cage is warded against spells. Mine, at least. Not against keys.
Their guard keeps the key at his hip. I've had a long time to observe.
I would pay you, but they took my purse and most of my dignity.
Please mind the chalk on the floor. I have been working.
Floor {floor}. I'd have guessed deeper. Everything here is deeper than it looks.
Free me and I'll be useful. I know four ways to set a man on fire, and two of them are polite.
I have a theory about these levels. Let me out and I'll bore you with it on the way down.
Don't trust the doors here. They remember who closed them.
again: Ah. You again. My theory has improved.
The chalk is still drying. The key is still on the guard.
freed: Splendid. Now, the polite ways first.
After you. Strictly for scientific reasons.

prisoner_agnes.name: Sister Agnes
first: Peace to you. Forgive me if I don't rise. They chained my ankle.
I came down for the ones who never came up. I found more than I could carry.
The guard carries the key. He isn't cruel, only hungry.
If you're hurt, come closer. I can still do that much through the bars.
I prayed for a door to open. I didn't say which one. And here you are.
Free me and I'll keep you standing. It's all I have left to give, and it's enough.
Don't spend your anger on them. Save it for the way out.
Floor {floor}. We are far from any chapel. That only makes the prayers shorter.
There were four of us. Ask me about the others when we are somewhere with light.
Your hands are shaking. Mine did too, at first. It passes.
again: You came back. I hoped you would.
Still here. Still praying. The key is still with him.
freed: Walk. I'll be right behind you, with whatever you need.
Thank you. Now let me earn it.
